hints.title: Count how many selected factors produce x to the sixth
hints.body: In (1+kx2)7, each selection of kx2 contributes two powers of x. To obtain x6, select that term from exactly three of the seven brackets.
hints.recap: Match the required exponent before choosing the binomial index.
hints.pitfall: Selecting six copies of a term containing x squared would produce x to the twelfth.
hints.pause: Write the coefficient using the number of choices of three brackets.

recall.reminder: Match the required exponent before choosing the binomial index.

hints.title: Build the other coefficient independently
hints.body: For the second expansion, decide which brackets supply the required power of x. Every remaining bracket supplies the other term.
hints.recap: A coefficient includes the combination count and all factors supplied by the remaining brackets.
hints.pitfall: Only cancel a parameter power after checking the stated nonzero condition.
hints.pause: Find both full coefficients, equate them and solve for the permitted parameter.

recall.reminder: A coefficient includes the combination count and all factors supplied by the remaining brackets.

solution:
1. Select the first coefficient. The x6 term in (1+kx2)7 uses three copies of kx2, giving coefficient (73)k3=35k3.

2. Select the second coefficient. The x6 term in (k+x)10 uses six copies of x and four copies of k, giving (106)k4=210k4.

3. Equate and cancel. 35k3=210k4. Since k≠0, we obtain 35=210k, so k=35210=16.

Answer A. No full expansion is needed.
